findings.title: Bracketed IPv6 host from uri.host is not a connectable address
findings.evidence: Net::HTTP.start is called with 'uri.host, uri.port' (8-space arg line). For a URL like https://[::1]:8443/x, URI.parse keeps the brackets, so uri.host is '[::1]' and TCPSocket/getaddrinfo fails with SocketError, which is not in RETRYABLE_ERRORS, so the call dies instead of fetching.
findings.recommendation: Use uri.hostname (bracket-stripped) for Net::HTTP.start, or reject bracketed hosts explicitly with a clear ArgumentError; add a test with an IPv6 literal URL.

findings.title: URI.parse errors and nil-host HTTPS URIs escape as the wrong exception type
findings.evidence: Only URI.parse is called with no rescue; a malformed URL raises URI::InvalidURIError rather than the ArgumentError the method advertises, and 'https:///path' parses as URI::HTTPS with a nil host, so uri.host is nil and Net::HTTP.start(nil, ...) fails with TypeError/SocketError after the https check has already passed.
findings.recommendation: Wrap URI.parse in a rescue converting URI::InvalidURIError to ArgumentError, and add an explicit nil/empty host check (raise ArgumentError unless uri.hostname && !uri.hostname.empty?) before building the request.

findings.title: Non-2xx (including redirects) raised as bare RuntimeError with host only
findings.evidence: The code branches on 'unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPSuccess)' and then raises a plain RuntimeError string containing only the status code and uri.host; callers cannot rescue a specific class, the path/query is dropped from the message, and ordinary 301/302/307 responses to a fetch helper become hard errors with no way to inspect Location.
findings.recommendation: Raise a dedicated error class (e.g. HttpFetch::HTTPError) carrying status, code and the full uri, and either follow a bounded number of redirects or document that 3xx is an error with a test pinning the behaviour.

findings.title: Retryable set omits common transient transport failures
findings.evidence: RETRYABLE_ERRORS lists only Net::OpenTimeout, Net::ReadTimeout and Errno::ECONNRESET; a truncated response (EOFError end of file reached), Errno::ECONNREFUSED/EHOSTUNREACH during a rolling restart, Errno::EPIPE, or OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError handshake failure are equally transient for an idempotent GET yet abort on the first attempt, so the bounded retry rarely helps in practice.
findings.recommendation: Extend the list with EOFError, Errno::ECONNREFUSED, Errno::EPIPE and OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError (require openssl), or accept a configurable retryable set; cover it with a test that stubs each class once and then succeeds.

findings.title: No tests for retry bound, non-retryable status, or scheme rejection
findings.evidence: The bound is 'raise if attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS'; the retry loop, the ArgumentError for non-https URLs, and the fact that an HTTP-status RuntimeError is not retried are all unverified, and the change ships no test file.
findings.recommendation: Add tests that (a) stub three Net::ReadTimeout raises and assert exactly 3 attempts and one re-raise, (b) assert a 500/301 is raised once with no sleep/retry, and (c) assert http:// and malformed URLs raise ArgumentError before any socket is opened.

findings.title: Only scheme is gated; internal HTTPS hosts reachable if callers pass untrusted URLs
findings.evidence: The guard checks only 'unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTPS)'; there is no host/IP allowlist or loopback/link-local block, so if any caller forwards user-controlled URLs this helper is an SSRF primitive against internal HTTPS endpoints (https-only does not prevent that). Dependency: only exploitable if operator/caller-supplied URLs can be attacker-influenced.
findings.recommendation: Either document that HttpFetch.get must only be given trusted URLs, or add an optional allowed-hosts/private-address rejection step before connecting, and note the trust assumption in the module comment.
